title: The 5 Longest Animals Ever Measured, Ranked (#1 Is a Worm)

scenes.text: The five longest animals on Earth, ranked. Number one is not a whale.

scenes.label: Fin whale · 27 m
scenes.text: Number five: the fin whale. Twenty-seven meters long, the second-longest whale there is.

scenes.label: Blue whale · 30 m
scenes.text: Number four: the blue whale. About thirty meters, the longest whale, and still shorter than the three below it.

scenes.label: Lion's mane jelly · 37 m
scenes.text: Number three: the lion's mane jellyfish. Its tentacles once stretched thirty-seven meters, longer than a blue whale.

scenes.label: Giant siphonophore · 47 m
scenes.text: Number two: a giant siphonophore filmed off Australia. About forty-seven meters of stinging, living chain, drifting in the deep.

scenes.label: Bootlace worm · 55 m
scenes.text: Number one: the bootlace worm. One was reported at fifty-five meters, a ribbon of slime on a North Sea beach.

description:
The five longest animals ever measured, ranked by length.
From the fin whale to a worm reported at 55 meters, longer than a blue whale.
Which of these would you least want to find on a beach?
first_comment: Which one would you least want to meet? And what should we rank next?
